lead: A cantilever slab is fixed at one edge and free at the other: it carries a hogging moment at the support, so its main steel goes at the top. A continuous slab runs over a row of beams, and the code gives its design moments from a table of coefficients instead of analysing every live-load pattern. A sunshade and a corridor floor are the two cases. Both are one-way slabs designed by limit state.
prereq: You need: the one-way slab strip and limit state flexure design from Chapter 4.1 and Unit 2.

sections.h3: Cantilever slab: moment at the face, steel at the top

blocks.text: A cantilever slab is fixed at one edge and free at the other: a chajja, a shop canopy, a small balcony. It bends down under load, so the top fibre stretches. Tension is at the top, so the main steel lies near the top face and runs back into the slab behind the support.

Design a 1 m wide strip. A load of w kN/m² on that strip is the same number in kN/m, because the strip is 1 m wide. Self weight is 25t kN/m², where t is the thickness in metres and 25 kN/m³ is the unit weight of reinforced concrete.

blocks.where: Mu is the hogging moment at the face of the support, per metre width, in kN·m/m; wu is the total factored load in kN/m² (the same number in kN/m on a 1 m strip); l is the clear projection from the face of the support to the free edge, in metres.

items: Take l from the face of the support to the free edge, never to the beam centre. IS 456 uses clear projection plus half the effective depth as effective length; the face still governs the moment.
Add self weight, finish and live load; multiply by 1.5 for wu.
Choose the thickness so l/d stays within the basic 7 for a cantilever, adjusted by the modification factor for the steel area.
Find Ast for Mu; check it against 0.12 per cent of the gross area for Fe415 steel.
Place the bars at the top, spacing not more than the smaller of 3d and 300 mm.
Run the top bars into the back span at least the development length Ld beyond the face.
Check shear at a distance d from the face, where V = wu (l − d).

sections.h3: Continuous slabs and the code moment coefficients

blocks.text: A slab cast over a row of parallel beams is continuous over the supports. An exact analysis needs several arrangements of live load, one per critical section. IS 456 gives coefficient tables for continuous beams, which a 1 m strip of slab uses directly.

blocks.where: Mu is the design moment at the section considered, per metre width, in kN·m/m; α is the coefficient read from the code table for that section and span type; wu is the total factored load in kN/m²; l is the effective span in metres.

items: Spans differ by not more than 15 per cent of the longest span.
The load is uniformly distributed over the whole slab.
The cross-section is the same in all spans.
No concentrated load the tables do not cover.

blocks.text: The tables already contain pattern loading. The largest sagging moment in a span comes with live load on that span and on alternate spans, dead load everywhere. The largest hogging moment at a support comes with live load on the two spans on either side of it. Designing each section for the worse case gives the moment envelope.

Top steel near a support follows that envelope. The hogging moment falls away from the support, so part of the top steel can be curtailed, keeping at least half running into the span and carrying every curtailed bar beyond the cut-off point by the anchorage length.

sections.h3: Where the two cases bite in detailing

blocks.text: In a cantilever the support is the whole design. The top bars must be anchored into the back span for a full development length, because bond over that length carries the hogging moment at the face. If the projection is short and the back span narrow, bend the bars down into the beam. Add distribution steel at right angles to the main bars.

In a continuous slab the steel follows the envelope: bottom bars at midspan, top bars over every support, heavier next to an end support. Top bars over an interior support usually run from the two adjacent spans and must reach far enough on both sides for bond.

figure.caption: A cantilever carries its moment at the support and holds the main steel at the top; a continuous slab takes its moments from the code coefficients, and the top steel follows the envelope and is partly curtailed.

spec.title: Cantilever and continuous slab
spec.aria: A chain of five boxes: cantilever slab with M = wl squared by 2 at the face, steel at the top anchored into the support, continuous slab with code coefficients, moment envelope for support and midspan, and top steel near the support partly curtailed.

examples.question: A cantilever slab projects 1.5 m clear from the face of a beam. Live load 3.0 kN/m², floor finish 1.0 kN/m², thickness 150 mm, M25 concrete, Fe415 steel, clear cover 20 mm, 10 mm main bars. Find the hogging moment at the support and the main steel. Then state how a three-span continuous slab of 3.0 m each, carrying the same loads, is designed by the coefficient method.
steps: Self weight = 25 × 0.150 = 3.75 kN/m². Total service load w = 3.75 + 1.0 + 3.0 = 7.75 kN/m².
wu = 1.5 × 7.75 = 11.625 kN/m², which is 11.625 kN/m on a 1 m strip.
l = 1.5 m to the face. Mu = 11.625 × 1.5²/2 = 13.078 kN·m per metre.
d = 150 − 20 − 5 = 125 mm. Mu/(fck b d²) = 13.078 × 10⁶/(25 × 1000 × 125²) = 0.0335, so the section is under-reinforced.
Solving Mu = 0.87 fy Ast d (1 − Ast fy/(b d fck)) gives Ast = 301.9 mm²/m. Minimum steel = 0.12% of 1000 × 150 = 180 mm²/m, so 301.9 mm²/m governs.
Provide 10 mm bars at 250 mm centres: 314.16 mm²/m, below the smaller of 3d = 375 mm and 300 mm. Capacity is 13.59 kN·m/m, greater than 13.078.

Shear at d from the face: V = 11.625 × (1.5 − 0.125) = 15.98 kN/m, τv = 15.98 × 10³/(1000 × 125) = 0.128 MPa. The code shear strength for M25 at this steel is higher, so no shear reinforcement is needed.
Development length Ld = φ × 0.87 fy/(4 τbd) = 10 × 361/(4 × 2.24) = 403 mm into the back span beyond the face.
l/d = 1500/125 = 12 against a basic 7 for a cantilever; even with the modification factor the limit is near 10, so 150 mm is shallow and 175 mm is the right choice.
Continuous slab: wu l² = 11.625 × 3.0² = 104.6 kN·m per metre. Check the three-span and 15 per cent conditions, read α at each section, and take Mu = α × 104.6 kN·m/m.
Design the steel at each section as in Chapter 4.1, keep top steel over every support, and curtail it where the envelope falls, carrying each curtailed bar beyond the cut-off by the anchorage length.
examples.answer: Mu = 13.078 kN·m per metre at the face; Ast = 301.9 mm²/m, so 10 mm bars at 250 mm centres at the top (314.16 mm²/m). At d from the face V = 15.98 kN/m and τv = 0.128 MPa, so no shear reinforcement is needed. The 1.5 m cantilever is shallow at 150 mm and better at 175 mm.
examples.check:
import math
b = 1000.0
t = 150.0
cover = 20.0
phi = 10.0
d = t - cover - phi/2
fck = 25.0
fy = 415.0
w = 0.150*25 + 1.0 + 3.0
wu = 1.5*w
l = 1.5
Mu = wu*l**2/2
ratio = Mu*1e6/(fck*b*d**2)
A = 0.87*fy*d
B = 0.87*fy**2/(b*fck)
Ast = (A - math.sqrt(A**2 - 4*B*Mu*1e6))/(2*B)
min_steel = 0.0012*b*t
Ap = math.pi*phi**2/4/0.250
cap = (0.87*fy*Ap*d - B*Ap**2)/1e6
V = wu*(l - d/1000)
tau_v = V*1000/(b*d)
tau_bd = 2.24
Ld = phi*0.87*fy/(4*tau_bd)
print(w)
print(wu)
print(round(Mu, 3))
print(d)
print(round(ratio, 4))
print(round(Ast, 2))
print(round(min_steel, 1))
print(round(Ap, 2))
print(round(cap, 2))
print(round(Ld, 2))
print(round(tau_v, 3))

traps: Measuring the cantilever span to the centre of the support instead of the face. The hogging moment is critical at the face.
Putting the main steel of a cantilever at the bottom. Tension is at the top, so bottom steel is wasted and the slab cracks at the support.
Using the code coefficients with only two spans, with spans differing by more than 15 per cent of the longest, or under a heavy concentrated load.
Adding separate pattern-load cases on top of the coefficients. They already include pattern loading; the design moments are the envelope.
Curtailing top steel in a continuous slab without the anchorage length beyond the cut-off, so the bar pulls out before it can develop its force.

quiz.q: Where is the main steel of a cantilever slab placed, and why?
quiz.a: Near the top face. The hogging moment at the support puts the top fibre in tension.

quiz.q: Which code tables give the moment coefficients for continuous beams and slabs?
quiz.a: The bending moment coefficient tables of IS 456, one for three spans and one for four or more; a 1 m strip of slab uses them directly.

quiz.q: Why does the code require the spans to be nearly equal before the coefficients may be used?
quiz.a: The coefficients come from the analysis of equal spans. A much longer span attracts a different share of moment, and the tabulated values no longer bound the real moments.

quiz.q: A cantilever slab projects 1.2 m clear, thickness 120 mm, floor finish 1.0 kN/m², live load 2.5 kN/m². Find the factored hogging moment at the face and the minimum steel.
quiz.a: Self weight = 25 × 0.12 = 3.0 kN/m²; w = 6.5 kN/m²; wu = 9.75 kN/m²; Mu = 9.75 × 1.2²/2 = 7.02 kN·m/m. Minimum steel = 0.12% × 1000 × 120 = 144 mm²/m.

quiz.q: For a four-span continuous slab, which spans carry live load to give the largest sagging moment in the second span?
quiz.a: Live load on the second span and on the fourth, with dead load on all spans. Alternate loading lets the loaded span sag without the neighbours holding it up.

quiz.q: Why does the largest hogging moment at a support occur when live load acts only on the two spans next to that support?
quiz.a: Those two spans bend down and rotate the slab over the support, pulling the top fibre there. Loading the further spans would stiffen the region and reduce the hogging.

quiz.q: A designer measures a 1.5 m cantilever to the centre of a 300 mm wide beam and designs for the larger moment. Is the design safe and economical?
quiz.a: Safe in flexure, because the moment is overestimated, but wasteful in steel; it also puts the anchorage check on the wrong section, and the true force at the face may not be developed if the bar is cut short.

beyond: Not for the exam. In practice a continuous slab is modelled in a frame analysis program with pattern loading, and the code coefficients act as a check on the output. Flat slabs need the frame method or the direct design method, and yield line theory gives the collapse load for irregular panels.
